extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, maintenance personnel, repair stations, and FAA certification/inspector staff
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and complying with Federal Aviation Administration airworthiness directives (ADs) specifying inspection, repair, replacement, recordkeeping, and alternative compliance procedures for specific airplane and helicopter models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect tail rotor gearbox for metal contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) If no metal contaminants are found return the tail rotor gearbox to service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If metal contaminants are found, follow the AD's required corrective actions (implied: remove/repair/replace). If none, the gearbox may be returned to service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace tail rotor gearbox within time-in-service limit
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Within 1,200 hours’ time in service since the last overhaul, remove and replace the tail rotor gearbox with an airworthy gearbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory replacement deadline measured in hours TIS since last overhaul; use an 'airworthy' gearbox (i.e., conforming, serviceable part).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approve alternate method of compliance through FAA manager
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) An alternate method of compliance with this AD, which provides an equivalent level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Chicago Aircraft Certification Office, FAA...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for AMOCs must be approved by the named FAA manager; contact/address provided in AD for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special flight permits to a base for maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) In accordance with Sections 21.197 and 21.199, flight is permitted to a base where the maintenance required by this AD may be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special flight permits may be issued to allow flight to a maintenance base solely for compliance with the AD, per FAR 21.197/21.199.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitive inspections for disbonding and corrosion of fuselage doublers
rubrics_metrics.description: This amendment requires repetitive inspections for disbonding and corrosion; ... and repair, if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the referenced Airbus Service Bulletin procedures and the AD-specified intervals and affected fuselage sections; repair actions must follow the service bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eddy current and ultrasonic inspections of fuselage longitudinal lap joints
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires eddy current and ultrasonic inspections of the fuselage longitudinal lap joints for cracks; and repair, if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the inspection methods (eddy current, ultrasonic) and the inspection areas and intervals as specified in the Airbus service bulletin and the AD. Detection of cracks requires repair prior to further flight as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial eddy current inspection of 'special' longitudinal lap joint areas
rubrics_metrics.description: A.1.a Prior to the accumulation of 24,000 landings, or within 10 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, perform an eddy current inspection in special areas of the longitudinal lap joints, in accordance with paragraph 2.B. of the service bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no cracks found, repeat at intervals not to exceed 6,000 landings (A.1.b). If cracks detected, repair prior to further flight per the service bulletin (A.1.c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial eddy current inspection of 'standard' longitudinal lap joint areas
rubrics_metrics.description: A.2.a Prior to the accumulation of 32,000 landings, or within 10 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, perform an eddy current inspection of the standard areas of the longitudinal lap joints, in accordance with paragraph 2.B. of the service bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no crack is found, repeat inspections at intervals not to exceed: (1) 6,000 landings for joints with bonded doublers; (2) 8,000 landings for joints without bonded doublers. If a crack is found, repair prior to further flight in accordance with the service bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspections of modified or repaired longitudinal lap joint areas per thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: A.3.a Prior to the accumulation of the threshold values (landings since first flight) identified in Tables 1 or 2 of the service bulletin, or within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, perform an eddy current inspection... in accordance with paragraph 2.B. of the service bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no crack is found, repeat inspections at intervals not to exceed 6,000 landings for each repair solution identified; if a crack is found, repair prior to further flight per the service bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect fuselage bonded inner doublers (Sections 13–18) for disbonding and corrosion
rubrics_metrics.description: B. Prior to the accumulation of 24,000 landings or 15 years since new, whichever occurs first, or within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, inspect fuselage bonded inner doublers of longitudinal lap joints in Sections 13 through 18 (except Sections 16 and 17 at Stringer 31 left-hand and right-hand) for disbonding and corrosion, in accordance with Airbus Industrie Service Bulletin A300-53-229...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1. If no disbonding or corrosion is found in areas other than Sections 13 and 14, no further action is required in those areas. 2. If disbonding or corrosion is found in Sections 13 and 14, repeat inspections at intervals not to exceed 12,000 landings or 8 years since last inspection. 3. If disbonding detected, repair prior to further flight per the service bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect Sections 16 and 17 at Stringer 31 for disbonding and corrosion with age threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: C. Prior to the accumulation of 24,000 landings or 12 years since new, whichever occurs first, or within 60 days after the effective date of this AD, whichever occurs later, inspect fuselage bonded inner doublers of longitudinal lap joints in Sections 16 and 17 at Stringer 31 left-hand and right-hand for disbonding and corrosion... Airplanes older than 12 years must be inspected within 12 months after the effective date of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no disbonding or corrosion is found, no further action is required. If disbonding is detected, repair prior to further flight in accordance with the service bulletin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate means of compliance routed through PMI to FAA manager
rubrics_metrics.description: D. An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Standardization Branch, ANM-113, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region. Note: The request should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI)...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMOC requests should be forwarded through the PMI, who will concur or comment and send to the Manager; AMOCs must provide equivalent level of safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special flight permits for Airbus AD compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: E. Special flight permits may be issued in accordance with FAR 21.197 and 21.199 to operate airplanes to a base in order to comply with the requirements of this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FAR 21.197/21.199 procedures to obtain permits to ferry aircraft to maintenance facilities for AD compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time inspection of MDHC engine-to-transmission driveshaft couplings
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Within the next 25 hours’ time in service or within 120 days after the effective date of the AD, whichever occurs first, inspect the couplings, MDHC Part Number (P/N) 369H5660, to determine serial numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required one-time inspection to identify potentially affected serial-numbered parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace specified coupling serial numbers with airworthy parts
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Replace any couplings, P/N 369H5660, which have serial numbers in the range from 5200 through 5309, with airworthy parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate replacement required for couplings in the specified serial-number range; use serviceable/airworthy replacement parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record compliance and serial numbers in maintenance records
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Record compliance with paragraph (a) of this AD in the AD compliance record and in the maintenance record of the helicopter log book. This record must include the serial numbers of any deficient couplings found during compliance with this AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AD compliance entries must document inspections and serial numbers of deficient parts; keep both AD compliance record and maintenance log updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark and purge unairworthy couplings from spares inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: Unairworthy couplings removed from service and in spares inventory should be marked unairworthy. Unairworthy couplings should be purged from spares inventory in accordance with MDHC SIN HN-216, DN-157, EN-47, FN-35, dated April 5, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label removed defective parts and remove from spares stock per the manufacturer's Service Information Notice procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardness test of welded lug of sponson truss components within 100 hours TIS
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Within the next 100 hours’ time in service after the effective date of this AD, conduct a hardness test of each welded lug of sponson truss tube assemblies ... as follows:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct specified laboratory or field hardness test procedures on listed P/Ns to determine whether hardness is within approved ranges; AD was amended to extend compliance times where appropriate based on service experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic fluorescent/visual inspections of sponson truss assemblies at landing-based intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Prior to the accumulation of 1,000 landings after the effective date of this AD, and thereafter at intervals not to exceed those landing intervals stated in Table 1, inspect the sponson truss tube assemblies for cracks in the locations noted in the table...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1 specifies inspection intervals (e.g., 2,500 and 4,700 landings) and exact inspection locations (tube-to-fitting welds, welded manufacturing holes, lug holes, clevis, etc.). The AD allows longer intervals than earlier versions where service experience shows equivalent safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend compliance times when service experience supports equivalent safety
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment extends the compliance times to alleviate difficulties experienced in accomplishing the hardness test and fluorescent penetrant inspections. The extended compliance times will eliminate unnecessary burdens on operators but, at the same time, provide an equivalent level of safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAA may revise AD compliance times when service data indicate inspections/tests require more time or spare parts are scarce, provided equivalent safety is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect cracks in DC-9 control columns via dye penetrant or eddy current per service bulletin
rubrics_metrics.description: A. ... perform a dye penetrant or eddy current inspection of both control columns ... in accordance with McDonnell Douglas DC-9 Alert Service Bulletin A27-288, Revision 3, dated July 6, 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial inspection scheduling is based on accumulated landings as of a reference date; use the service bulletin methods (including added ultrasonic method) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial inspection schedule based on accumulated landings (DC-9)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators determine initial inspection timing based on each airplane's accumulated landings as of the AD's reference date. Subsequent repetitive intervals are specified separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitive inspection interval for DC-9 control columns
rubrics_metrics.description: B. For all airplanes: If no cracks are found, accomplish repetitive inspections in accordance with paragraph A., above, at intervals not to exceed 3,800 landings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repetitive inspections must follow the same inspection method as initial inspection and be conducted within the maximum interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable corrective actions for cracked DC-9 control columns before further flight
rubrics_metrics.description: C. If crack(s) are found in either control column ... accomplish one of the following before further flight: 1. Blend out the cracks up to depths of 0.030 inch, maintaining minimum thickness ... and continually inspect at intervals not exceeding 3,800 landings, until replacement procedures are accomplished; or 2. Remove the cracked control column ... and replace it with a new production control column ...; or 3. Repair in a manner approved by the Manager, Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blending is limited to a max depth and must maintain minimum wall thickness per the service bulletin/table and requires ongoing inspections until terminating action. Replacement parts and service bulletins are referenced. Repairs require FAA manager approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement as terminating action (DC-9)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. Replacement of the Captain’s and First Officer’s control column ... with new control columns ... constitutes terminating action for the requirements of this amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installing the specified new-production control columns ends the requirement for the repetitive inspections mandated by this AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair or replacement must be accomplished prior to further flight
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph C. of the final rule has been revised to clarify that repair or replacement of cracked control columns must be accomplished prior to further flight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a crack is detected, the aircraft is not permitted to fly further until one of the specified corrective actions has been completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of alternate compliance methods subject to FAA approval via PMI
rubrics_metrics.description: E. An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Los Angeles Aircraft Certification Office, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region. Note: The request should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI)...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMOC procedure repeated across ADs: requests routed through PMI for FAA review and approval; must provide equivalent level of safety.
